newsitem.title: FRANCE: Huge cannabis haul headed for Britain, Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Huge cannabis haul headed for Britain, Netherlands.

text.p: A 20-tonne container of Colombian cannabis seized in France in one of Europe's biggest drugs hauls had been destined for the Netherlands and Britain, a police chief said on Tuesday.

French chief anti-drugs policeman Gilles Leclair told a news conference the drug, with a street value of 200 million francs ($40 million), was loaded last month in the Colombian port of Buenaventura on the freighter Humboldt Express bound for Bilbao in Spain, Le Havre in France and Antwerp in Belgium.
French police, acting on a tip-off from Colombian and Spanish police, set up a trap after the container, listed as a shipment of jeans, was taken to a depot near Rouen.
They detained a Colombian, two Belgians and a Frenchman last Friday. Police announced the haul on Monday.
Leclair said the Colombian was believed to be a senior member of the Cali drugs cartel. "Someone who takes delivery of 20 tonnes of drugs cannot be very far from the top," he said.
Leclair said the seizure was the second biggest ever made in Europe after a 23.8-tonne haul of Colombian cannabis made by Dutch police last year.

A court in the southwest city of Toulouse meanwhile ordered the release of three Italians detained in January 1994 when French customs seized 1.2 tonnes of cocaine - a seizure police then described as "the haul of the century".
The three Italians said on leaving court they were tricked by French undercover agents and did not know they were transporting cocaine when they brought the haul into France.
The court said that customs officers had failed to disclose initially that they had infiltrated the drugs ring and possibly ordered the delivery themselves as a trap for major smugglers.
Under French law, narcotics agents are required to say they have infiltrated a drugs ring when the case comes to court.

The court was told the cocaine was flown from Cali and dropped off French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America where it was picked up by a Honduran-registered vessel which carried it to France.
